title: Balancing Chemical Equations
guideH2O: Water forms from hydrogen and oxygen gas. Adjust the coefficients until every H and O atom matches on both sides.
guideNH3: Ammonia is made from nitrogen and hydrogen gas — the basis of many fertilizers. Balance the N and H atoms.
guideFe2O3: Iron rusts by combining with oxygen gas. Balance the Fe and O atoms to match real rust chemistry.
guideCombustion: Methane burns in oxygen to release energy. Balance the carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atoms on both sides.
coefficientsHint: Set each coefficient (1–6) so atom counts match on both sides.
playbackHint: Press Play to watch the atoms gently rearrange as the reaction proceeds.
learnMore: Balanced equations show the Law of Conservation of Mass — atoms rearrange during a reaction, but none are created or destroyed.
quizQuestion: Why do we balance chemical equations?
quizCorrect: To conserve the number of atoms (mass) on both sides
quizWrong: To make the equation look neater
